items.t: Short-term relief of occasional constipation.

src.q: For the short-term relief of occasional constipation

items.t: MHRA: use stimulant laxatives only if bulk-forming and osmotic laxatives are ineffective. Children under 12 should not use them without advice from a prescriber; 12-17 years can be supplied under pharmacist supervision.

src.q: stimulant laxatives should only be used if other laxatives (bulk-forming and osmotic) are ineffective

Stimulant laxatives should no longer be used in children under 12 years without advice from a prescriber, while products for children aged 12 to 17 years can be supplied under the supervision of a pharmacist.

items.t: Use only if diet change or bulk-forming agents fail.

src.q: This product should only be used if a therapeutic effect cannot be achieved by a change of diet or the administration of bulk forming agents.

items.t: Adults (and over 12 years with the 12-plus product): 1-2 tablets at night; start low and use the smallest dose that gives a soft-formed motion. The 12-plus SmPC: a higher dose may be prescribed under medical guidance, up to a maximum of 30 mg hydroxyanthracene glycosides a day.

src.q: Adults, the elderly and children over 12 years: Swallow one to two tablets at night
A higher dose may be prescribed under medical guidance.
The maximum daily dose of hydroxyanthracene glycosides is 30 mg.
The correct individual dose is the smallest required to produce a comfortable soft-formed motion.

items.t: Duration: one UK SmPC says use for more than 1-2 weeks needs medical supervision; the adult-labelled pack SmPC says not more than 1 week (usually 2-3 doses in that week).

src.q: Use for more than 1-2 weeks requires medical supervision.
Not to be used for more than 1 week. Usually it is sufficient to take this medicinal product up to two to three times during that week.

items.t: If no bowel action after 3 days of increasing dose, consider medical examination.

src.q: If no bowel action has occurred after three days of progressively increased dosage, a medical examination should be considered.

items.t: 12-plus product: contraindicated under 12 years.

src.q: Children under 12 years of age.
Should not be used in children or adolescents under the age of 12 years (see section 4.3).

items.t: Adult-labelled pack: should not be used under 18 years.

src.q: Should not be used in children or adolescents under the age of 18 years.

items.t: MHRA: children under 12 should not use stimulant laxatives unless told to by their prescriber.

src.q: children younger than 12 years should not use stimulant laxatives without advice from a prescriber and clinical guidance should be followed

items.t: Hypersensitivity to senna or any excipient.

src.q: 4.3 Contraindications Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients.

items.t: Use at the same time as other laxatives.

src.q: Not to be used at the same time as other laxative agents.

items.t: Intestinal obstruction and stenosis, atony, appendicitis, inflammatory bowel disease (e.g. Crohn's, ulcerative colitis), abdominal pain of unknown origin, severe dehydration with water and electrolyte depletion.

src.q: Cases of intestinal obstructions and stenosis, atony, appendicitis, inflammatory bowel diseases (e.g Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis), abdominal pain of unknown origin, severe dehydration state with water and electrolyte depletion

items.t: Pregnancy and lactation.

src.q: Pregnancy and lactation (see section 4.6 and 5.3).

items.t: Children under 12 years (12-plus product).

src.q: Children under 12 years of age.

items.t: Patients on cardiac glycosides, antiarrhythmics, QT-prolonging medicines, diuretics, corticosteroids or liquorice root must consult a doctor before use.

src.q: Patients taking cardiac glycosides, antiarrhythmic medicinal products, medicinal products inducing QT-prolongation, diuretics, adrenocorticosteroids or liquorice root, have to consult a doctor before taking senna leaf preparations concomitantly.

items.t: Do not use with faecal impaction or undiagnosed acute or persistent GI complaints (pain, nausea, vomiting) unless advised by a doctor: possible ileus.

src.q: should not be taken by patients suffering from faecal impaction and undiagnosed, acute or persistent gastro-intestinal complaints, e.g. abdominal pain, nausea and vomiting, unless advised by a doctor

items.t: Avoid long-term use: impaired bowel function, laxative dependence, atonic colon; prolonged excessive use can cause fluid/electrolyte imbalance and hypokalaemia.

src.q: Long-term use of stimulant laxatives should be avoided, as use for more than a brief period of treatment may lead to impaired function of the intestine and dependence on laxatives.
Prolonged excessive use may lead to fluid and electrolyte imbalance and hypokalaemia.

items.t: Where dehydration may be harmful (e.g. renal insufficiency, elderly) and fluid is lost: stop and restart only under medical supervision.

src.q: In patients suffering from fluid loss where dehydration may be harmful (e.g. renal insufficiency, elderly patients) Senokot should be discontinued and only be restarted under medical supervision.

items.t: Galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption: should not take (contains lactose).

src.q: Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, the Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take this medicine.

items.t: Stimulant laxatives do not help with weight loss.

src.q: Stimulant laxatives (including Senokot) do not help with weight loss.

items.t: Other laxatives: must not be used at the same time (SmPC 4.3).

src.q: Not to be used at the same time as other laxative agents.

items.t: Hypokalaemia from long-term laxative abuse potentiates cardiac glycosides and interacts with antiarrhythmics and QT-prolonging medicines.

src.q: Hypokalaemia (resulting from long-term laxative abuse) potentiates the action of cardiac glycosides and interacts with antiarrhythmic medicinal products
and with medicinal products inducing QT-prolongation.

items.t: Other hypokalaemia-inducing medicines (e.g. diuretics, corticosteroids, liquorice root) may enhance electrolyte imbalance.

src.q: Concomitant use with other medicinal products inducing hypokalaemia (e.g. diuretics, adrenocorticosteroids and liquorice root) may enhance electrolyte imbalance.

items.t: Kidney disorders: be aware of possible electrolyte imbalance. In renal insufficiency with fluid loss, stop and restart only under medical supervision.

src.q: Patients with kidney disorders should be aware of possible electrolyte imbalance.
(e.g. renal insufficiency, elderly patients) Senokot should be discontinued and only be restarted under medical supervision.

items.t: No hepatic impairment dosing advice. Chronic overdose of anthranoid-containing medicines may cause toxic hepatitis.

src.q: Chronic ingested overdoses of anthranoid containing medicinal products may lead to toxic hepatitis.

items.t: SmPC: contraindicated in pregnancy (genotoxicity data for some anthranoids).

src.q: The use during pregnancy is contraindicated because of experimental data concerning a genotoxic risk of several anthranoids, e.g. emodin and aloe emodin.

items.t: BUMPS (differs from the SmPC): a laxative can be used in pregnancy if diet and lifestyle fail; stimulant laxatives such as senna are tried only when other types have not helped. Concern about womb contractions has not been seen in pregnant women.

src.q: Stimulant laxatives only tend to be tried when those above have not helped.
However, this has not been observed in pregnant women.

items.t: SmPC: contraindicated during lactation (active metabolites such as rhein pass into milk in small amounts).

src.q: The use during lactation is contraindicated because after administration of anthranoids, active metabolites, such as rhein, were excreted in reast milk in small amounts.

items.t: SPS (differs from the SmPC): standardised senna can be used during breastfeeding; as a precaution monitor the infant for diarrhoea or irritability.

src.q: Standardised senna preparations can be used during breastfeeding.
As a precaution monitor the infant for diarrhoea or irritability.

reproductive.note: UK SmPC: no data on fertility.

items.t: Frequency not known: abdominal pain, cramps, diarrhoea (especially with irritable colon; reduce dose); harmless yellow or red-brown urine discolouration.

src.q: Abdominal pain2, abdominal spasm2, diarrhoea2
Yellow or red-brown (pH dependent) discolouration of urine by metabolites, which is not clinically significant, may occur during the treatment.

items.t: Chronic use: colonic mucosal pigmentation (pseudomelanosis coli), usually reversible on stopping.

src.q: Chronic use may cause pigmentation of the intestinal mucosa (pseudomelanosis coli), which usually recedes when the patient stops taking the preparation.

items.t: Hypersensitivity, urticaria, asthma.

src.q: Hypersensitivity, urticaria, asthma, hypogammaglobulinaemia

items.t: Hypokalaemia from prolonged use with diarrhoea; chronic use may cause water/electrolyte disorders, albuminuria and haematuria. Overdose: severe diarrhoea with fluid and potassium loss; replace fluids and monitor potassium.

src.q: Prolonged use of laxatives resulting in diarrhoea and subsequently hypokalaemia.
Electrolytes, especially potassium, should be monitored.

items.t: Daily laxative need or persistent abdominal pain: see a doctor and investigate the cause.

src.q: If laxatives are needed every day, or abdominal pain persists, a doctor should be consulted.

items.t: Overdose or abuse: monitor electrolytes, especially potassium (particularly in the elderly).

src.q: Electrolytes, especially potassium, should be monitored. This is especially important in the elderly.

items.t: Swallow 1-2 tablets at night. Effect usually after 8-12 hours.

src.q: Swallow one to two tablets at night
Defaecation takes place after a delay of 8 - 12 hours

items.t: Do not exceed the stated dose. If no bowel movement after 3 days, or symptoms worsen, see a doctor or pharmacist.

src.q: Do not exceed the stated dose.
If the symptoms worsen during the use of the medicinal product or there is no bowel movement after three days, a doctor or pharmacist should be consulted.

items.t: Does not help with weight loss; overuse can be harmful.

src.q: Does not help with weight loss. Overuse can be harmful.

items.t: Urine may turn yellow or red-brown; this is harmless.

src.q: Yellow or red-brown (pH dependent) discolouration of urine by metabolites, which is not clinically significant
